core_obligations: Invoke the Leray spectral sequence for $\mathcal{G} \mapsto H^p(\mathcal{Y}, R^q f_{QCoh,*}\mathcal{G}) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{G})$ from the cited sites-cohomology result (proof lines 2312-2318).

Identify the E_2 page with $H^p(\mathcal{Y}, R^q f_*\mathcal{G})$: the adjunction morphism $R^q f_{QCoh,*}\mathcal{G} \to R^q f_*\mathcal{G}$ has parasitic kernel and cokernel (cited adjoint-kernel-parasitic), and parasitic modules have vanishing cohomology (cited pushforward-parasitic), hence the map induces an isomorphism on cohomology (proof lines 2320-2330).
proof_roadmap: Recall the Leray spectral sequence for the qc derived pushforward.
Show the natural comparison map on E_2 pages is an isomorphism by killing kernel and cokernel, which are parasitic.
difficulty_reason: The argument combines the Leray spectral sequence from sites-cohomology with the parasitic-kernel/cokernel mechanism: the adjunction map between the two derived pushforwards has parasitic kernel and cokernel, whose cohomology vanishes, so the E_2 pages agree and the spectral sequences identify.
